integrity: The claim is proved analytically from an explicit two-outcome measurement and the published data-processing property of maximal quantum f-divergence. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The counterexample is for rank-one singular states and \(f(t)=t\log t\). It refutes the all-state interval-range assertion but does not claim failure of the faithful-state theorem or of the endpoint values in this example.
title: Pure states collapse the maximal \(t\log t\) unitary-orbit range to two values
